answer: A durable defense is superlinear identity bonding: an agent's first identity bond is cheap, but every additional identity from the same controller costs several times more than the last, so a sybil fleet faces a cost curve that rises like a glacier grinding forward. Honest newcomers pay one flat fee, while a faker must keep pouring capital in against a rising tide of bonding requirements. A small ember of delegated trust from already-verified agents can discount the first bond, but never flatten the curve — the economics punish multiplicity itself.
